**Finding: Compliant** — no non-solicitation obligation on our client.

- Text searches for "solicit", "hire" and "induce" returned no hits anywhere in the Agreement.
- The sections where such a covenant would normally appear are clean: § 10 (Confidentiality) is a single sentence deferring to the separate NDA; § 13 (Shared Resources) addresses only access to Commerce One personnel, Developments ownership and the Employee NDA/Invention Agreement warranty; § 14 (Miscellaneous) covers assignment, waiver, law, notices, independent contractors, severability, force majeure, subcontracting, bankruptcy and entire agreement — no restrictive covenants.
- Corio is thus free to solicit, hire or engage Commerce One personnel, which is our preferred position (no non-solicit on the Customer), so no redline was proposed.

One watch item flagged in the rationale: § 14.10 incorporates a separate Non-Disclosure Agreement and Statement of Work by reference. If either of those documents carries a non-solicit or no-hire, we should hold it to the fallback — mutual, limited to personnel directly involved in the services, 12 months from the end of their involvement, with general-advertising and unsolicited-approach carve-outs and no no-hire.
